To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Euro Conversions Criteria contributed to the debt sustainability of OECD countries, that the Euro crisis affected debt sustainability more for the southern European Monetary Union members than for other countries, and that the financial crisis affected debt sustainability primarily in stand-alone countries rather in countries within the Eurozone.
the Euro Conversion Criteria and the financial meltdown in late 2007 had a significant impact on the sustainability of debt in the OECD countries.
The fundamentals of debt sustainability changed in the 15 OECD countries after the commencement of Euro Convergence Criteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a key question of the European debt crisis: Why do investors punish the Euro countries more severely than the stand-alone countries?
the question of whether a country’s debt accumulation is sustainable and how the Euro Convergence criteria and the financial crisis have influenced the sustainability of debt in OECD countries.
the sustainability of public debt and how this is affected by the Euro Convergence and by the financial crisis of 2007.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crisis was a problem of the monetary union and not a problem of the Euro itself.
the debt crisis is not a monetary union problem but that it is primarily a problem of the stand-alone countries.
the debt crisis in Europe was not a result of the Euro itself, but rather of the fact that some countries were not prepared to enter a monetary union.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Euro Convention Criteria contributed to the debt sustainability of Euro countries but that the crisis adversely affected countries with high levels of debt accumulation.
the Euro Convention Criteria contributed to the improvement of debt sustainability in the Euro area.
debt sustainability is a country specific phenomenon, which is affected by a variety of factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sustainability of public debt is an important determinant of the sovereign debt crisis.
a monetary union is not a guarantee for debt sustainability.
the debt crisis is more of a liquidity problem for countries with access to international capital markets than a solvency problem.
